ja: 宇宙に長く滞在すると、背骨の間が広がって身長が数cm伸びる。地球に戻ると元に戻る。
easy: In space, astronauts grow a few centimeters taller. They go back to normal on Earth.
std: Astronauts can grow a few centimeters taller in microgravity as their spines lengthen, returning to normal back on Earth.

ja: 月は1年に約3.8cmずつ地球から遠ざかっている。
easy: The moon moves about 3.8 cm farther from Earth every year.
std: The Moon is moving away from Earth at about 3.8 centimeters per year.

ja: 月はいつも同じ面を地球に向けている。裏側を人類が初めて見たのは1959年、ソ連の探査機の写真だった。
easy: We always see the same side of the moon. People first saw the far side in a 1959 photo.
std: The Moon always shows the same face to Earth; the far side was first photographed by the Soviet probe Luna 3 in 1959.

ja: 夜空でいちばん明るい恒星は、おおいぬ座のシリウス。
easy: Sirius is the brightest star in the night sky.
std: Sirius, in the constellation Canis Major, is the brightest star in the night sky.

ja: 天の川銀河には、1000億〜4000億個の恒星があると推定されている。
easy: Our galaxy, the Milky Way, has 100 to 400 billion stars.
std: The Milky Way is estimated to contain between 100 and 400 billion stars.

ja: 光は1秒間に約30万km進む。地球を7周半する速さ。
easy: Light travels about 300,000 km in one second. That is seven and a half times around the Earth.
std: Light travels about 300,000 kilometers per second, fast enough to circle the Earth seven and a half times in a second.

ja: 地球の大気は、約78％が窒素、約21％が酸素でできている。
easy: Earth's air is about 78% nitrogen and 21% oxygen.
std: Earth's atmosphere is about 78 percent nitrogen and 21 percent oxygen.

ja: 水は4℃のとき最も重く（密度が高く）なる。そのため冬の湖は表面から凍り、底の水は凍りにくい。
easy: Water is heaviest at 4°C. That is why lakes freeze from the top.
std: Water is densest at about 4°C, which is why lakes freeze from the top down and the bottom stays liquid.

ja: 地球の北極と南極（磁極）は、過去に何度も入れ替わってきた。最後の入れ替わりは約78万年前。
easy: Earth's magnetic north and south have switched many times. The last time was about 780,000 years ago.
std: Earth's magnetic field has reversed many times; the most recent reversal occurred about 780,000 years ago.

ja: 音は空気中を秒速約340mで進むが、水中では約4倍、鉄の中ではさらに速く伝わる。
easy: Sound moves about 340 meters per second in air. It is about four times faster in water.
std: Sound travels at about 340 meters per second in air, roughly four times faster in water and faster still in steel.

ja: 地球の自転は少しずつ遅くなっており、1日の長さは100年でおよそ1.7〜2ミリ秒長くなっている。
easy: Earth is spinning a little more slowly over time. Days are getting longer very slowly.
std: Earth's rotation is gradually slowing, lengthening the day by roughly 1.7 to 2 milliseconds per century.

ja: ハッブル宇宙望遠鏡は1990年に打ち上げられた。最初はレンズ（主鏡）の形にわずかなずれがあり、1993年に宇宙飛行士が修理した。
easy: The Hubble telescope went to space in 1990. Its mirror had a problem, and astronauts fixed it in 1993.
std: The Hubble Space Telescope launched in 1990 with a flawed mirror, which astronauts corrected during a servicing mission in 1993.

ja: 地球に落ちてくる隕石の多くは、火星と木星の間の小惑星帯から来ている。
easy: Most meteorites come from the asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter.
std: Most meteorites that reach Earth originate in the asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter.

ja: ハレー彗星は約76年ごとに地球に近づく。次に見られるのは2061年ごろ。
easy: Halley's Comet comes near Earth about every 76 years. The next time is around 2061.
std: Halley's Comet returns roughly every 76 years; its next appearance is expected in 2061.

ja: 原子のほとんどは空っぽの空間。原子核は原子全体のごく一部で、原子をサッカー場にたとえると、原子核はその中央の小さな豆粒ほど。
easy: Atoms are mostly empty space. If an atom were a stadium, the center would be like a small pea.
std: Atoms are mostly empty space: if an atom were the size of a stadium, its nucleus would be about the size of a pea.

ja: 周期表を作ったのはロシアのメンデレーエフ（1869年）。まだ見つかっていない元素の性質まで予言した。
easy: Mendeleev made the periodic table in 1869. He even guessed elements no one had found yet.
std: Dmitri Mendeleev published his periodic table in 1869 and predicted the properties of elements not yet discovered.

ja: 113番元素ニホニウムは、日本の理化学研究所が発見し、2016年に名前が決まった。アジアで初めて命名された元素。
easy: Element 113, nihonium, was found by Japanese scientists. It was named in 2016.
std: Element 113, nihonium, was discovered by Japan's RIKEN and named in 2016, the first element named by an Asian country.

ja: 雲は水蒸気そのものではなく、とても小さな水や氷の粒が集まったもの。
easy: Clouds are not water vapor. They are tiny drops of water or ice.
std: Clouds are not made of water vapor itself but of countless tiny droplets of water or ice crystals.

ja: 金のような重い元素の多くは、中性子星どうしの合体などで作られたと考えられている。
easy: Gold was probably made when very heavy dead stars crashed together.
std: Much of the universe's gold is thought to have been forged in violent events such as neutron star mergers.

ja: 細胞（cell）という言葉は、1665年にロバート・フックが顕微鏡でコルクを見て、小部屋のようだと名付けた。
easy: Robert Hooke used the word 'cell' in 1665. Cork under a microscope looked like small rooms.
std: Robert Hooke coined the term 'cell' in 1665 after seeing cork under a microscope; its compartments reminded him of small rooms.

ja: ゾウは鏡に映った自分を自分だと認識できる数少ない動物の一つ。
easy: Elephants can know themselves in a mirror. Few animals can do this.
std: Elephants are among the few animals shown to recognize themselves in a mirror.

ja: ミツバチは「8の字ダンス」で、仲間に花のある方向と距離を伝える。
easy: Honeybees dance to tell other bees where to find flowers.
std: Honeybees perform a 'waggle dance' to tell nestmates the direction and distance of food sources.

ja: コウテイペンギンのオスは、真冬の南極で何も食べずに約2か月、足の上で卵を温め続ける。
easy: Male emperor penguins keep their egg warm on their feet for about two months without eating.
std: Male emperor penguins incubate their egg on their feet through the Antarctic winter for about two months without eating.

ja: キリンの首の骨の数は7個で、人間と同じ。1つ1つの骨がとても長い。
easy: Giraffes have seven neck bones, the same as people. Each bone is just very long.
std: A giraffe has seven neck vertebrae, the same number as humans; each one is simply very long.

ja: ラッコは眠るとき、流されないように海藻を体に巻きつけたり、仲間と手をつないだりする。
easy: Sea otters hold hands or wrap seaweed around themselves so they do not float away while sleeping.
std: Sea otters wrap themselves in kelp or hold paws while resting so they don't drift apart.

ja: ニューカレドニアガラスは、枝を加工して道具を作り、木の中の虫を取り出す。
easy: New Caledonian crows make tools from sticks to get insects out of trees.
std: New Caledonian crows craft tools from twigs and leaves to extract insects from crevices.

ja: シロナガスクジラは地球史上最大級の動物で、心臓だけで数百kgある。
easy: The blue whale may be the biggest animal ever. Its heart weighs hundreds of kilograms.
std: The blue whale is the largest animal known to have lived, with a heart weighing several hundred kilograms.

ja: ウミガメの赤ちゃんの性別は、卵がある砂の温度で決まる。温かいとメスが多くなる。
easy: For sea turtles, the sand's temperature decides if babies are male or female. Warm sand makes more females.
std: In sea turtles, nest temperature determines sex: warmer sand produces more females.

ja: アメリカのセコイアの仲間には、高さ110mを超える木があり、世界で最も背の高い木とされる。
easy: The tallest tree in the world is a redwood in the US. It is over 110 meters tall.
std: The tallest known living tree is a coast redwood in California, more than 110 meters tall.

ja: 竹には1日に1m近く伸びる種類もある。
easy: Some kinds of bamboo can grow almost one meter in a day.
std: Some bamboo species can grow nearly a meter in a single day.

ja: 地球上のアリの数は約2京匹（2万兆匹）と推定されている（2022年の研究）。
easy: A 2022 study says there are about 20 quadrillion ants on Earth.
std: A 2022 study estimated that about 20 quadrillion ants live on Earth.

ja: ハチドリは空中で止まったり、後ろ向きに飛んだりできる。
easy: Hummingbirds can stay still in the air and even fly backward.
std: Hummingbirds can hover in place and even fly backward.

ja: フクロウは首を約270度回すことができる。
easy: Owls can turn their heads about 270 degrees.
std: Owls can rotate their heads about 270 degrees.

ja: コアラは1日に約18〜22時間眠る。主食のユーカリの葉は栄養が少なく、消化にエネルギーがかかるため。
easy: Koalas sleep about 20 hours a day. Their food gives them little energy.
std: Koalas sleep around 18 to 22 hours a day, as their eucalyptus diet provides little energy.

ja: サケは生まれた川のにおいを覚えていて、海で数年過ごした後、同じ川に戻ってくる。
easy: Salmon remember the smell of the river where they were born. They come back years later.
std: Salmon return from the ocean to spawn in the same river where they hatched, guided largely by smell.

ja: 北アメリカのオオカバマダラは、数千kmを渡ってメキシコで冬を越す。往復には数世代かかる。
easy: Monarch butterflies fly thousands of kilometers to Mexico for the winter.
std: Monarch butterflies migrate thousands of kilometers to overwinter in Mexico, a round trip that spans several generations.

ja: 日本のソメイヨシノは、ほとんどが接ぎ木で増やされたクローンなので、同じ地域ではほぼ一斉に咲く。
easy: Most Somei-Yoshino cherry trees in Japan are clones, so they bloom at almost the same time.
std: Japan's Somei-Yoshino cherry trees are largely clones propagated by grafting, which is why they bloom almost simultaneously in a given area.

ja: ニシオンデンザメは数百年生きると考えられ、脊椎動物で最も長生きとされる。
easy: The Greenland shark may live for hundreds of years. It is the longest-living animal with a backbone.
std: The Greenland shark may live for several centuries, making it the longest-lived known vertebrate.

ja: キョクアジサシは北極と南極の間を毎年往復し、渡りの距離は動物で最も長い。
easy: The Arctic tern flies between the Arctic and the Antarctic every year.
std: The Arctic tern migrates between the Arctic and Antarctic each year, the longest migration of any animal.

ja: キノコは植物より動物に近い仲間と考えられている。
easy: Mushrooms are more closely related to animals than to plants.
std: Fungi, including mushrooms, are more closely related to animals than to plants.

ja: エジプトのクフ王のピラミッドは、約3800年にわたって世界で最も高い人工建造物だった。
easy: The Great Pyramid in Egypt was the tallest building in the world for about 3,800 years.
std: The Great Pyramid of Giza was the tallest human-made structure in the world for about 3,800 years.

ja: イギリスのオックスフォード大学で教育が行われていた記録は1096年までさかのぼる。アステカ帝国の成立（1428年）より古い。
easy: Oxford University is older than the Aztec Empire.
std: Teaching at Oxford dates back to at least 1096, making the university older than the Aztec Empire, founded in 1428.

ja: 万里の長城は一つの壁ではなく、何世紀にもわたって作られた多くの壁の集まり。宇宙から肉眼で見えるという話は誤り。
easy: The Great Wall of China is many walls built over centuries. You cannot see it from space with your eyes.
std: The Great Wall is a series of walls built over many centuries; the claim that it is visible to the naked eye from space is a myth.

ja: イギリスのマグナ・カルタ（1215年）は、王の権力も法に従うという考えの出発点とされる。
easy: Magna Carta, from 1215, said that even the king must follow the law.
std: Magna Carta, sealed in 1215, is seen as an early step toward the principle that rulers are subject to the law.

ja: グーテンベルクは1450年ごろ活版印刷を実用化し、ヨーロッパで本が一気に広まった。
easy: Gutenberg's printing press, around 1450, helped books spread quickly in Europe.
std: Johannes Gutenberg's movable-type printing press, developed around 1450, made books far more widely available in Europe.

ja: 江戸幕府は約260年続き、その間、大きな戦争のない時代が長く続いた。
easy: The Edo period in Japan lasted about 260 years and was mostly peaceful.
std: The Tokugawa shogunate ruled Japan for about 260 years, a long era largely free of major wars.

ja: 1853年、アメリカのペリーが黒船で浦賀に来航し、日本の開国のきっかけとなった。
easy: In 1853, Commodore Perry came to Japan with black ships. This led Japan to open its doors.
std: In 1853 Commodore Matthew Perry arrived at Uraga with his 'black ships', setting in motion the opening of Japan.

ja: 日本初の鉄道は1872年、新橋〜横浜間で開業した。
easy: Japan's first railway opened in 1872, between Shimbashi and Yokohama.
std: Japan's first railway opened in 1872 between Shimbashi in Tokyo and Yokohama.

ja: 自由の女神像はフランスからアメリカへの贈り物で、1886年に完成した。
easy: The Statue of Liberty was a gift from France to the US. It was finished in 1886.
std: The Statue of Liberty was a gift from France to the United States and was dedicated in 1886.

ja: エッフェル塔は1889年のパリ万博のために作られた。当初は20年後に取り壊す予定だった。
easy: The Eiffel Tower was built for a world fair in 1889. It was supposed to stay only 20 years.
std: The Eiffel Tower was built for the 1889 World's Fair and was originally meant to be dismantled after 20 years.

ja: ライト兄弟の初飛行（1903年）は12秒間、約37mだった。
easy: The Wright brothers' first flight in 1903 lasted 12 seconds and went about 37 meters.
std: The Wright brothers' first powered flight, in 1903, lasted 12 seconds and covered about 37 meters.

ja: ベルリンの壁は1961年に作られ、1989年11月に崩壊した。翌1990年にドイツは統一された。
easy: The Berlin Wall was built in 1961 and fell in 1989. Germany became one country again in 1990.
std: The Berlin Wall was built in 1961 and fell in November 1989; Germany was reunified in 1990.

ja: 国際連合は1945年、51か国で発足した。今の加盟国は193か国。
easy: The United Nations started in 1945 with 51 countries. Now it has 193.
std: The United Nations was founded in 1945 with 51 member states and now has 193.

ja: 日本の国名を「日本」と定めた時期は7世紀後半〜8世紀初めごろとされ、それ以前は「倭」と呼ばれていた。
easy: Japan started using the name 'Nihon' around the late 600s. Before that, it was called 'Wa'.
std: The name Nihon came into use around the late seventh or early eighth century; earlier Chinese records called the country Wa.

ja: 『源氏物語』は11世紀初めに紫式部が書いた。世界最古級の長編小説とされる。
easy: 'The Tale of Genji' was written by Murasaki Shikibu in the early 1000s. It is one of the oldest novels.
std: The Tale of Genji, written by Murasaki Shikibu in the early 11th century, is often called one of the world's first novels.

ja: 百年戦争（イギリスとフランス）は、実際には1337年から1453年までの116年間続いた。
easy: The Hundred Years' War between England and France really lasted 116 years.
std: The Hundred Years' War between England and France actually lasted 116 years, from 1337 to 1453.

ja: ナポレオンは背が低かったとよく言われるが、実際は約169cmで、当時のフランス人としては平均的だった。
easy: Napoleon was not very short. He was about 169 cm, normal for his time.
std: Napoleon is often said to have been short, but at about 169 centimeters he was of average height for his time.

ja: イースター島のモアイ像は約900体あり、多くは13〜16世紀ごろに作られたとされる。
easy: Easter Island has about 900 large stone statues called moai.
std: Easter Island has nearly 900 moai statues, most carved between about the 13th and 16th centuries.

ja: マチュ・ピチュは15世紀にインカ帝国が築いた都市で、1911年に世界に広く知られるようになった。
easy: Machu Picchu is a city built by the Inca in the 1400s. The world learned about it in 1911.
std: Machu Picchu, built by the Inca in the 15th century, became widely known to the outside world in 1911.

ja: 伊能忠敬は50歳を過ぎてから測量を学び、約17年かけて日本全国を歩いて正確な地図を作った。
easy: Ino Tadataka started learning at age 50. He walked across Japan for 17 years to make an exact map.
std: Ino Tadataka began studying surveying after 50 and spent about 17 years walking across Japan to produce remarkably accurate maps.
